title: TUTTI: Parallel CKKS Bootstrapping in under 3 ms on CPU
summary: This paper introduces TUTTI, a new CKKS bootstrapping procedure that outperforms previous low-latency solutions in multi-threaded latency for any number of messages and, most notably, has a lower latency than TFHE when bootstrapping a single one. Our bootstrapping builds upon SPRU (CK, TCHES 2027), improving it with new methods for exploiting parallelism and increasing the number of messages, as well as with a refined security analysis, of independent interest, of the block-binary secret keys of LMSS (AsiaCCS 2023). TUTTI bootstraps 4096 real-number messages in 46 to 83.4 ms on 192 threads to restore 1 to 9 multiplicative levels, outperforming SHIP (CHKS, Eurocrypt 2025) by a factor of up to 3 on the same machine. Unlike SHIP, TUTTI gains immediately from bootstrapping fewer messages, with a 256-message bootstrapping taking just 15 to 34 ms on 32 threads. For a single message, TUTTI takes 4.6 ms on 32 threads, whereas TFHE-rs needs 7.3 ms for a 4-bit bootstrapping on the same machine and thread count. We show that this advantage persists across different architectures: on an Apple M5 Pro laptop (ARM), TUTTI takes 2.4 ms on 14 threads, against 4.5 ms for TFHE-rs. Differences between
